method: Individual contextual reading of PDF pages 11–15. Definitions explain recorded language, not actual insurance entitlements. Suspect transcript wording is preserved, not verified against audio.
words: a person or company hired under a contract to do particular work
contract + -or names the person or company doing contracted work. Stress CON- in contractor.
We hired a contractor to repair the building.
我们聘请了承包商来修缮这栋楼。
A best dose contractors appears in the PDF; asbestos contractors is a plausible intended reading, but remains unverified and is not substituted into the quotation.
the process of getting rid of unwanted material
dispose of means get rid of; disposal names that process. Replace final e in dispose with -al.
The facility handles the safe disposal of waste.
这家设施负责废物的安全处置。
Waste-management sense, not arrangement or classification.
discarded material that can cause harm to people or the environment
hazard + -ous describes danger; combine it with waste, material no longer wanted. Remember the whole chain hazardous waste disposal.
The containers are used to store hazardous waste.
这些容器用于储存危险废物。
Explains the comparison in a statistic the narrator explicitly says is not verified.
the possibility of loss, harm, or another unwanted result
Connect risk with risky: adding -y describes something involving risk. Remember worth the risk when weighing a possible loss.
The shortcut was not worth the risk.
抄这条近路不值得冒这个险。
Insurance exposure in the discussion; no ranking is established as fact.
a numerical fact or figure about a group or situation
被广泛引用的统计数据
One numerical figure is a statistic; a collection is statistics. Stress -TIS-, and attach the word to a number with a source.
We could not verify the widely cited statistic.
我们无法核实这项被广泛引用的统计数据。
The speaker disputes the source and exact ranking; the example preserves that uncertainty.
the intoxicating substance in drinks such as beer or wine; such drinks collectively
Picture beer and wine under the same alcohol label. Learn the three syllables AL-co-hol and connect them with alcoholic drinks.
The event rules restrict alcohol consumption.
Drinking-rule context, not the broad organic-chemistry class. Essay in the same source sentence is not translated as 散文.
a person serving on a group that directs an organization
a board member of the organization
Board here is a governing group, not a plank; member is a person in it. Picture people sitting around a boardroom table.
A board member explained the proposal.
一位理事会成员解释了这项提议。
A representative of the organization is quoted; the statement is not independently verified policy guidance.
a local branch of a larger organization
A book has chapters; a large organization has local chapters. The shared image is one part of a larger whole, not a book section here.
The local chapter meets every month.
地方分会每月举行一次会议。
Chapter houses are fraternity branch houses, not chapters of a book.
small text containing detailed conditions or restrictions
Fine can mean small or delicate; fine print is the small writing where conditions may be hidden. Picture enlarging the bottom of a contract.
Read the fine print before signing.
签字前请阅读小字条款。
Restrictions in the narrator's policy example; not attractive typography.
a male student social organization at a college or university
Connect fraternity with fraternal, meaning brotherly; the spoken shortening is frat. Stress -TER-.
He joined a fraternity in his first year.
他大一时加入了一个兄弟会。
College organization sense; the discussion generalizes and explicitly does not apply to every organization.
humiliating or harmful treatment imposed on people joining a group
入会欺凌；羞辱性入会仪式
haze drops final e before -ing: hazing. Link the verb haze new members with the noun hazing; do not confuse it with misty haze.
The university introduced rules to prevent hazing.
大学制定了防止入会欺凌的规定。
Initiation practices in the source, not ordinary teasing or fog.
a business that provides insurance policies
an insurance company pays a claim
保险公司赔付一项索赔
Insure gives insurance; company identifies the business providing it. Connect the provider with the policy rather than treating insurance as a verb.
Contact your insurance company about the claim.
请就这项索赔联系你的保险公司。
Big fraternities means large organizations, not 大兄弟; teaching example avoids copying the bad machine translation.
legal responsibility for harm, damage, or a debt
liable becomes liability: change -able to -ability. Being liable means having responsibility, not merely being likely to do something.
The agreement explains liability for damage.
协议说明了损害赔偿责任。
Recorded insurance/legal vocabulary only; not an assessment of who is actually liable.
insurance protection for specified liabilities to other people
Liability is the responsibility; coverage is the insurance protection. Keep the two roles separate when remembering liability coverage.
The company reviewed its liability coverage limits.
公司审查了责任险的保额限额。
Write coverage is insurance-industry usage for providing/issuing cover; actual terms depend on a policy, not this narration.
operating or existing across a country rather than only locally
nation + -al gives national. Contrast a national organization with its local chapter to fix the scope.
The national office supports local chapters.
全国总部为地方分会提供支持。
National organization does not mean a state agency or 国家组织 here.
a very difficult, unpleasant, or worrying situation
噩梦般的难题；棘手局面
A nightmare is a frightening dream; extend that image to an unpleasant situation. Insurance nightmare is figurative, not a dream about sleep.
Organizing transport became a logistical nightmare.
安排交通成了一个后勤上的大难题。
Risk-management problem involving student houses, not a literal nightmare.
a group of people with an established structure and common purpose
organize becomes organization: replace final e with -ation. People organize their work within an organization.
She helps run a nonprofit organization.
她协助运营一家非营利组织。
An institution, not the quality of being orderly.
retaining financial risk instead of transferring all of it to an insurer
自行承担保险风险的；自保的
self + insuring means taking the insurance risk on oneself. Insure drops final e before -ing.
The organization considered self-insuring against small losses.
该组织考虑自行承担小额损失的风险。
Source conflates self-insurance and setting up insurers; define the term carefully without validating that explanation. Resulted in in the PDF is not silently changed to resorted to.
providing an additional layer of insurance protection above specified underlying coverage
Imagine a large umbrella above existing cover. The metaphor helps recall umbrella coverage, not a physical umbrella to buy for rain.
They asked about an umbrella policy.
他们咨询了一份伞式保险保单。
Insurance modifier; replaces the misleading 雨伞 translation. No advice that a particular policy is required or sufficient.
pieces of cloth used to cover the eyes and prevent seeing
blind + fold evokes cloth folded over the eyes. Add plural -s pronounced /z/ after /d/.
The players removed their blindfolds after the game.
游戏结束后，参与者取下了蒙眼布。
A noun fragment in the hazing discussion; do not translate it as an imperative to blindfold someone.
inter- means between; personal concerns people. Interpersonal connects two or more people, unlike intrapersonal within one person.
The role requires strong interpersonal skills.
这个岗位要求较强的人际交往能力。
Speaker's praise of friendship is sarcastic in context, not approval of harmful initiation.
the status of belonging to an organization
member + -ship names the status, as friendship names a relationship. The member is the person; membership is belonging.
她的会员资格下个月到期。
Membership loss is part of the narrator's hypothetical account, not a universal policy rule.
a contract stating the terms of insurance protection
Policy has several senses: company policy is a rule, insurance policy is a contract. Anchor this card to insurance policy and its written terms.
Read the exclusions in your insurance policy.
请阅读保险合同中的除外条款。
Corrects government/company-rule definition and example to the actual insurance-contract sense.
behavior in which someone enjoys exercising control over others excessively
滥用权力以满足控制欲
开始滥用权力满足控制欲
Trip is figurative here: imagine someone carried away by a sense of power. Learn on a power trip, not a journey to gain electricity.
He seemed to be on a power trip during the meeting.
他在会上似乎一味想摆权威、控制别人。
Negative evaluation of the person overseeing initiation, not a literal 权力之旅.
rescind ends in /d/, so rescinded adds /ɪd/. Connect it with the earlier verb card rescind and an official cancellation stamp.
他的成员资格被撤销了。
Official withdrawal in a hypothetical example; stress restored.
a list of people invited or allowed to enter an event
A guest is an invited person; a guest list records those people. Keep guest singular when it modifies list.
Please check the guest list at the entrance.
请在入口处核查宾客名单。
Event entry context, not a list of hotel rooms.
Connect inebriate with inebriated and inebriation. This formal word can be replaced by drunk in everyday conversation; stress NEE, not NEB.
这位宾客看起来喝醉了。
Corrects erroneous /nɛ/ pronunciation. No individual capacity or medical diagnosis is inferred.
protected under an insurance policy for specified risks
有保险保障的；已投保的
insure + d gives insured. Contrast insured, protected by a policy, with assured, reassured or confident.
Check that the vehicle is insured.
Staying insured in the narrator's explanation; actual scope of coverage not established.
a rule or condition that restricts something
limit becomes limitation, turning the boundary into a noun for a restriction. Picture a line marking the maximum allowed amount.
There is a limitation on the number of guests.
Quantity restriction on drinks, not a personal inability.
strikingly expressive or fitting, as if part of a story or poem
有诗意的；（此处）颇有讽刺意味、像戏剧般巧合的
几乎像诗一样意味深长的
poet → poetic connects with poetry. In almost poetic, picture an outcome so neatly fitting that it feels scripted; context can make the comment ironic.
There was something almost poetic about the coincidence.
这个巧合颇有一种意味深长的巧妙感。
Sarcasm follows membership being dropped after initiation; poetic is not inherently a synonym for ironic.
a person or organization separate from the principal parties involved
Party can mean a participant, not a celebration. A third party is outside the two main sides; hyphenate third-party before vendor.
An independent third party reviewed the process.
独立第三方审查了这一流程。
Outside service provider, not a third social gathering.
a person or business that sells goods or provides services
vend means sell; -or names the seller. Connect vendor with vending machine, a machine that sells things.
We hired an approved vendor for the event.
我们为活动聘请了获准的供应商。
Event drinks/service provider in the source.
an alternative method used to get past a problem or restriction
work + around: instead of removing the obstacle, find a way around it. One workaround is a noun; work around is the verb phrase.
We found a temporary workaround for the software problem.
我们为这个软件问题找到了临时变通办法。
Narrator's label for arrangements about drinking, not a guarantee that they preserve coverage.
an internal rule governing an organization
组织内部规章；章程条款
Bylaw contains law, but here it is an organization's internal rule. Contrast a bylaw with a rule imposed on everyone by the state.
The club adopted a bylaw on membership fees.
俱乐部通过了一条有关会费的内部规章。
Fraternity-rule sense, not a municipal ordinance.
the internal rules governing an organization
bylaw + -s gives bylaws, with /z/ at the end. The plural often refers to the organization's complete set of rules.
Members voted to amend the bylaws.
成员们投票决定修订章程。
Plural preserved as a separate existing target; not municipal laws in this context.
designed to be very unlikely to fail or be used incorrectly
不容易出错的；稳妥可靠的
fool + proof: proof here means resistant to something, as in waterproof. Imagine a system that still works despite user mistakes.
We need a foolproof way to save the files.
我们需要一种不易出错的文件保存方法。
The speaker says the arrangements are not foolproof; no guaranteed protection claimed.
belonging or relating to a person who owns a home
home + owner + 's: the apostrophe marks possession, not a plural. Homeowners' would refer to several owners.
She checked her homeowner's insurance policy.
她查阅了自己的房主保险保单。
Possessive modifier in the source; the alleged payouts are not verified as generally available coverage.
a particular field of business or professional activity
Learn industry with industrial, but note that an industry can provide services as well as manufacture goods. Picture a whole field of businesses.
Industry experts discussed the new rules.
业内专家讨论了新规定。
Professional field, not the dictionary sense of diligence or hard work.
amounts of money paid, especially by an insurer in response to claims
pay out is the verb; payout is the noun. Add -s for multiple payments and retain the /ts/ ending.
The report listed the insurance payouts.
报告列出了各笔保险赔付款。
Distinguish compensation paid to claimants from fees paid to lawyers; the following discussion changes focus.
an act that breaks a rule or agreement
violate replaces final e with -ion to form violation. Learn violation of + rule or agreement.
The incident was treated as a violation of club rules.
这起事件被认定为违反俱乐部规定。
Breach of organization/policy terms in the quoted account; not all possible meanings of violation.
cases brought before a court by people or organizations against others
law + suit gives lawsuit, a legal action; plural -s makes lawsuits. A suit here is not clothing.
Fragment completes imagine the amount of; teaching model uses several/countable cases rather than copying disfluency.
brought a legal claim against someone in court; in passive use, faced such a claim
sue already ends in e, so add only d: sued. Contrast sued /sud/ with suit /sut/ by listening to the final consonant.
The company was sued for damages.
该公司被起诉要求赔偿损失。
Get sued is passive; does not imply the claimant won.
planned or arranged as a coordinated activity
organize + d gives organized. Here it describes a planned event, while an organized person is good at arranging things.
The volunteers attended an organized training session.
志愿者们参加了一场统一安排的培训。
Modifies meetups; comparison is the narrator's criticism, not a factual equivalence between all events.
alternative ways of dealing with problems or restrictions
workaround is one alternative route; workarounds are several. The plural ending is /z/ after /d/.
我们测试了两种可能的变通办法。
Two arrangements in the source; no implication that these always meet insurance conditions.
a person invited to an event or welcomed by a host
Pair guest with host: the host welcomes, the guest visits. Keep the final /st/ and distinguish guest from guess.
Each guest received a name tag.
每位来宾都领到了一张姓名牌。
Invited event attendee, not specifically a hotel customer.
beverage is a formal word for drink; its /dʒ/ ending takes plural /ɪz/. Count drinks, not types, in six beverages.
The cafe serves hot and cold beverages.
这家咖啡馆供应冷热饮品。
Six beverages refers to number of drinks, not 六种饮料; source lists beer/wine quantities as an example.
removes someone from a group, plan, or arrangement
取消某人的资格；将某人移出
Drop can mean let something fall; figuratively, drop someone from a plan removes them. Drops here is a verb, not plural droplets.
The organization drops members who stop paying fees.
该组织会取消不再缴费者的成员资格。
Corrects plural-of-drop definition and 退出 meaning: the organization removes the member, rather than the member voluntarily quitting.
to take on a duty or responsibility
Assume has two common senses: assume it is true means suppose; assume responsibility means take it on. Picture putting a responsibility on your own shoulders.
The team leader will assume responsibility for the project.
团队负责人将承担项目责任。
Responsibility-taking sense in assume the liability, not guessing or believing without evidence.
phrases: set up
to establish or start an organization or arrangement
建立；设立
They set up a small company together.
他们一起创办了一家小公司。
Establishing a company, not framing someone or physically arranging equipment.
came together
joined forces or gathered for a shared purpose
联合起来
Several local groups came together to organize the event.
几个本地团体联合起来组织了这场活动。
Organizations cooperating, not literal physical collision.
big names
well-known or influential people or organizations in a field
知名人士；业内大人物
Several big names in the industry attended.
几位业内知名人士出席了。
Reputation and prominence, not long names or body size.
take on
to accept responsibility for a task or case
承接；承担
Our team cannot take on another project this month.
我们团队这个月无法再接一个项目。
Lawyers accepting cases, not putting on clothing or confronting an opponent.
under certain circumstances
when particular conditions apply
在特定情况下
The fee can be waived under certain circumstances.
在特定情况下可以免收这笔费用。
Not every situation; maintains the qualification in the source's hypothetical explanation.
segments: Imagined insurer refusal continues 157; take your money means keep/take it elsewhere, not literal accepting payment.
Cover is insure, consistent with the refusal in 158, not physically cover.
Go through that means experience/deal with the trouble, not travel through an object.
chunk:3:it's not even worth the risk
Worth compares potential benefit with exposure; even adds emphasis to refusal.
Them points to organizations insurers allegedly refuse; no independent underwriting conclusion.

A best dose contractors is suspect ASR for asbestos contractors, but not audio-verified. Sixth worst statistic is explicitly questioned in subsequent paragraphs; do not silently correct or endorse it.
Attributes the statement to a magazine and immediately states there is no official list; prevents treating the preceding ranking as verified.
A best dose contract is another suspect ASR form; preserve exact PDF and await audio verification before proposing a quotation repair.
Mold is a specialized comparison in an uncertain asbestos exchange; no confident interpretation from one short sentence.
I see signals understanding, not literal vision.
Repeats the explicit absence of an official list.
Hard to say expresses uncertainty about the ordinal ranking, not difficulty speaking.
Exact source is the origin of the repeated statistic; speaker admits inability to verify it. Keep repeating is continue saying.
Unfinished alternative rank; uncertainty carried across the next paragraph.
Sororities needs the female student-organization sense; fraternity alone does not cover it.
Greek life is US fraternity/sorority culture, not life in Greece; needs an explicit learning item.
Just means only; narrows the disputed statistic to male organizations.
Does emphasizes appear, though marks concession; retains the narrator's inference rather than asserting an independently checked market fact.
Restates uncertainty about sixth worst while reporting the speaker's impression; pronouns refer to insurers and fraternities.
Insurance extension, not rain protection; source's an umbrella coverage is retained but teaching example uses an umbrella policy.
Repeats insurance phrase; no actual recommendation that any organization must purchase a particular product.
Like asks for a comparison with a company, not a preference.
Run means manage; right asks for confirmation of the organizational comparison.
National means country-wide parent organization, not government; usually qualifies the narrated claim.
Chapter houses are local branch houses; a bunch of is informal quantity; nightmare is figurative difficulty. Disfluent agreement is not copied into teaching example.
Acknowledges a comprehensible explanation, not independent agreement that insurance details are true.
Repeats the acknowledgment in 183; no additional language barrier is introduced.
False start followed by two nouns; countable lawsuits versus uncountable liability kept distinct in new teaching examples.
On a weekly basis means every week; cover incidents means respond financially under insurance, as the speaker alleges.
Resulted in self-insuring is printed wording; possible resorted to is unverified. Speaker also conflates retained risk with setting up insurers, so do not certify the explanation.
Set up means establish; card now supports the phrasal verb.
Came together means collaborated; big fraternities are large organizations, not older brothers.
Acronym expanded in the sentence; Trust is part of the organization's proper name. No independent fact-check of corporate status is claimed.
Write coverage is provide/issue insurance; roughly half is approximate. Things is completed by the relative clause in 192; claim remains attributed to board member.
Essay in list of grounds for suit is euphemistic/ASR wording, not written composition; retain source and flag. Other insurance claims remain attributed.
Fine print announces restrictions rather than small aesthetic print.
Pledged, vague, directed towards, and representative of need support; unfinished disclaimer continues in 195 and must not become an assertion about all organizations.
Completes the not representative disclaimer in 194; review with that full sentence before closing.
Introduces a hypothetical if scenario, not a report about a named member.
End up is eventual outcome; get sued is passive, not a judgment of liability.
Annual payment in the narrator's example; like qualifies an approximate amount.
Alternative rough amounts attributed to some people, not a verified fee schedule.
The minute means as soon as; under certain circumstances limits the hypothetical statement. No general insurance rule inferred.
Chains claimed consequences of membership cancellation and coverage loss; definition/example now use insurance policy, not company rules.
Anymore/no longer indicates ending the hypothetical membership.
Spanked is a concrete action in the initiation account and needs a definition; do not hide it behind a generic hazing label.
phrase:3:have a lot more in common with
Comparison with organized meetups conveys criticism; FetLife is a proper-name adult social platform reference, not a reusable learner word.
Noun fragment adds equipment to the preceding description; new example uses the correct noun meaning.
Raw onion, forced to plank, and professing undying love contain multiple concrete/idiomatic barriers needing explicit support; no coverage from theme alone.
You're big may be ASR for your big, a fraternity mentor role; do not repair without audio. Continues into 208.
Sarcastic praise after coercive actions; pinnacle remains a vocabulary gap and the opening attaches to uncertain 207.
Dropped means membership removed; court filing needs explicit support and the statement remains a generalized claim, not a verified rule.
Ironically fitting outcome after claimed membership cancellation, not simply beautiful poetry; contextual note distinguishes lexical meaning from sarcasm.
Workarounds names alternatives; odd marks the speaker's evaluation, not assurance that the arrangements are valid.
Long disfluent enumeration introduces option one; assume liability means accept responsibility, not guess. This is reported language, not insurance advice.
Host an event and stop giving drinks describe service roles; too inebriated means too drunk. Gonna is informal going to.
Liable is adjective related to liability, meaning responsible as asserted in the example; no determination of actual liability.
BYOB begins option two and is expanded in 216, but wording whole list of BYOB is unclear; read the full checklist before approving.
Source explicitly expands BYOB as beer. A checklist lists required steps; supposed to indicates expected compliance, not guaranteed behavior.
Assign someone at the door means designate an entry checker; incomplete task details supplied in 218–220.
Event-entry list, not an unspecified list of objects.
Age threshold in the narrator's scenario; not offered as current jurisdiction-specific legal advice.
It has to be marked has an unclear antecedent (list/eligibility); do not invent a specific mark or checking procedure.
Six drinks is a count, not six types; and under means at most. Limits are narrated examples, not validated policy terms.
Some sort of acknowledges imprecision about the limit rather than specifying a confirmed rule.
Band is likely a wristband used for entry/drinking controls, not musicians; needs an explicit contextual item. Cannot remove is covered by take off.
Restricts the quantity to what the attendee brought; like is a filler, not a comparison here.
Ensure in the PDF may stand for insure; retain the original and await audio rather than teaching ensure as insurance protection.
Short response to the preceding question; does not resolve its transcription uncertainty.
Fellow fraternity brothers and the contrast between checkers' ages and the stated threshold need explanation; no blanket coverage.
Not foolproof denies reliability; repeated it's is speech repair.
Which is why links the previous asserted weakness to the speaker's conclusion; nonstandard there's a lot of things is retained only in source.
Fallback transition, completed by the following discussion; not a standalone guarantee.
Disfluent question about who funds payments; referent of them and insurer/claimant relationships are unclear. Do not convert pays them out into a universal clean model.
If scenario asks consequences of losing coverage. Drops means organization removes the member, not member quitting or liquid drops.
Apparently limits confidence; payout and policy definitions clarify the attributed claim without treating parents' insurance as guaranteed coverage.
Unfinished evaluative reaction; continuation elaborates the impression rather than supplying missing factual content.
Ecosphere is a figurative interconnected professional world; take on cases means accept them, now taught with a transferable work example.
Big names means prominent professionals; heads are leaders, and profanity intensifies hate. No literal size or diligence sense.
Everybody knows everybody is hyperbole for a small connected circle, not a verified universal social network.
A Reddit user's quoted annual payment; per brother per year specifies both units and went to means was spent on. Attribution is not verification.
Either...or joins two alleged breaches; in which case refers back to that condition. Entire generalization is part of a user's quoted account, not binding policy interpretation.
Non-brothers means nonmembers, not unrelated siblings; athletic is a further vocabulary gap. Quoted policy account must remain attributed.
